INCIDENT 725253 - MINOR ENVIRONMENTAL INCIDENT - DEEP ENERGY - 081888C001 - SNORRE GIS - 05 AUGUST 21 - TELLUS 32 DISCHARGE DURING HOT STAB (FEMALE RECEPTACLE)
REMOVAL OF THE TEMPORARILY INSTALLED SUBSEA MATTRESS, COVERING THE PROJECT 14” PIPELINE
UPON COMPLETION OF THE REMOVAL OF THE MATTRESS TO THE WET STORE LOCATION, THE NEXT STEP INVOLVED THE REMOVAL OF THE PIPELINE TEMPORARY CAP
TO REMOVE THE TEMP. CAP ON THE 14” PIPE, XLX43 HAD TO INSTALL A HYDRAULIC STAB INTO THE FEMALE RECEPTACLE ON THE TEMP. CAP.
WITH THE STAB INSTALLED, XLX43, ATTEMPTED TO PRESSURISE THE INTERNALS OF THE PRESSURE CAP TO 300 BAR AS PER THE PIPELINE INSTALLATION PROCEDURE.
AT APPROX. 150 BAR PRESSURE, IT WAS OBSERVED ON THE MONITORS (CAMERA FROM XLX43) THAT THERE WAS A HYDRAULIC LEAK (BUBBLES), FROM BEHIND THE FEMALE RECEPTACLE ON THE HEAD OF THE TEMPORARY CAP.
IMMEDIATELY ONCE THE LEAK WAS OBSERVED, THE PUMP ON XLX43 WAS STOPPED, AND THE STAB WITHDRAWN TO CHECK THE INTEGRITY OF THE O RINGS.
THE O RINGS WERE FOUND TO BE SERVICEABLE. WITH THE O RINGS PROVED, THE HOT STAB WAS AGAIN REINSERTED, AS THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS ATTRIBUTED TO THE HOT STAB NOT SEATED FULLY.
THE MALE HOT STAB, WAS ONCE AGAIN REINSERTED INTO THE FEMALE RECEPTACLE, WHERE ONCE AGAIN THERE WAS A LEAK (BUBBLES) OBSERVED.
TO ASCERTAIN WHERE THE LEAK WAS COMING FROM, XLX43 WAS RECOVERED TO DECK, WHERE A FULL FUNCTION TEST WAS COMPLETED IN A BUNDENED WORK AREA, WHERE THE VEHICLE HELD PRESSURE (300BAR).
UPON THE FULL FUNCTION HAD BEEN CONDUCTED ON XLX43, THE VEHICLE WAS LAUNCHED SUBSEA, TO ONCE AGAIN PRESSURISE THE CAP.
UPON PRESSURISING THE FEMALE RECEPTACLE CAP, A FURTHER LEAK WAS OBSERVED. THE LEAK WAS DETERMINED/ OBSERVED TO BE COMING FROM THE PIPE WORK, OF THE, FEMALE RECEPTACLE.

THERE WAS NO INDICATION OF SMOKE OR OTHER ABNORMALITIES ON THE OTHER ENGINES AND BRIDGE WAS INFORMED ACCORDINGLY.

TASK/ACTIONS LEADING UP TO THE INCIDENT:_X000D_ _X000D_ ACCESS TO THE SKANDI VICTORIA DECK FOR THE DEEP BLUE WAS MID SHIPS BETWEEN THE 15T CRANE AND THE COMEN. THE SKANDI VITORIA HAD MOVED ONE 20' HALF HEIGHT CONTAINER FROM THE PORT SIDE TO A CENTRAL DECK AREA WITHIN REACH OF THE DEEP BLUE CRANE AND COMMENCED PREPARATION OF THE SECOND HALF HEIGHT CONTAINER FROM THE SAME AREA AS THE FIRST.

THE RIGGING SUPERVISOR REQUESTED THE WHIPLINE CRANE TO THE HALF HEIGHT CONTAINER WHERE A RIGGER HAD LEANED INTO THE HALF HEIGHT CONTAINER AND GRABBED THE 8T 1M SLING THAT WAS CONFIGURED IN A BASKET HITCH THROUGH THE MASTER LINK AND AWAITED THE CRANES ARRIVAL.

INCIDENT / INITIAL FINDINGS: _X000D_ _X000D_ THE CRANE WAS MANOEUVRED INTO POSITION CLOSE TO THE HALF HEIGHT CONTAINER EDGE HOWEVER DUE TO THE SHORT NATURE OF THE SLING IT DID NOT REACH THE HOOK WHEN ATTEMPTED SO THE RIGGER REQUESTED ADDITIONAL LENGTH ON THE CRANE WIRE FROM THE RIGGING SUPERVISOR WHO WAS IN CLOSE CONTACT. SOONER THAN ANTICIPATED THE CRANE WIRE PAID OUT AND AS THE HEADACHE BALL DESCENDED THE SHOULDER OF THE HEADACHE BALL MADE CONTACT WITH THE RIGGERS LEADING ARM HOLDING THE RIGGING CAUSING HIS WATCH DIAL TO PART FROM THE STRAP AND DROP INSIDE THE BASKET.
IMMEDIATE ACTIONS:_X000D_ _X000D_ IP REMOVED FROM DECK _X000D_ CRANE & WORKSITE MADE SAFE _X000D_ TIME OUT FOR SAFETY CONDUCTED.

INCIDENT 670728 - DAMAGE INCIDENT – 078773A001 ANNUAL RE-CERT – BERTH 4, IMPERIAL SOUTH. LEITH. 16/02/2020

INCIDENT: AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT THE VESSEL WAS STARBOARD SIDE TO THE QUAY, SITTING ON 2 YOKOHAMA FENDERS. MOORING ARRANGEMENT WAS 2X HEADLINES, 2X BREAST LINES AND 2X SPRINGS FORWARD. 2X STERN LINES, 2X BREAST LINES AND 2X SPRINGS AFT.
NOTE: DUE TO THE POSITION OF THE BOLLARD AND CONTROL MEASURES (SEGREGATION/COMMUNICATION) ON THE QUAYSIDE THERE WAS NO REALISTIC POSSIBILITY OF ANY INDIVIDUAL BEING IN THE LINE OF FIRE.

INITIAL FINDINGS: THE OUTER HULL OF THE VESSEL SUSTAINED SUPERFICIAL DAMAGE. SUBSEQUENT INSPECTION (17/02/2020) REVEALED THAT DAMAGE OCCURRED IN WB1 TANK WHERE DEFORMATION OF THE SIDE SHELL WAS EVIDENTT. APPROX 30MM DEEP OVER AN AREA OF 400MM X 400MM SQUARE.

CURRENT SITUATION: UPON HEARING THE IMPACT AGAINST THE SHIP’S HULL THE CAPTAIN IMMEDIATELY ATTENDED THE BRIDGE, AND INSTRUCTED THAT THE GANGWAY BE CLOSED. THE VESSEL THEN COMMENCED START-UP OF FORE AND AFT THRUSTERS. ONCE A FORWARD THRUSTER WAS ONLINE THIS WAS USED TO ARREST THE DRIFT AND THRUST THE BOW BACK TOWARD THE QUAY. AS FURTHER THRUSTERS WERE STARTED ADDITIONAL THRUST WAS APPLIED UNTIL THE VESSEL WAS STABILISED.
GIVEN THE CONTINUED SIGNIFICANT WIND GUSTS THE GANGWAY REMAINED CLOSED UNTIL THE CAPTAIN WAS SATISFIED THAT THE VESSEL WAS SUFFICIENTLY STABLE.
ON COMPLETION OF THE MOORING OPERATION THE THRUSTERS WERE KEPT RUNNING TO ASSIST WITH HOLDING THE VESSEL ALONGSIDE AND REDUCING THE WEIGHT ON THE SHORE SIDE BOLLARDS.
ONCE SUFFICIENT DAYLIGHT WAS APPEARANT, THE CAPTAIN & CHIEF ENGINEER ATTENDED THE QUAYSIDE TO INSPECT THE HULL AND BOLLARD.

THE BUOYANCY EFFECT OF SEAWATER NEEDS TO BE CONSIDERED.
SEAWATER HAS A DENSITY OF AROUND 1.025 G/CM3.
THE WEIGHT OF AN OBJECT IS EQUAL TO ITS MASS MULTIPLIED BY THE ACCELERATION DUE TO GRAVITY (9.81 M/S2).
TO CALCULATE THE WEIGHT OF 2.5 KG OF STAINLESS STEEL IN SEAWATER, FOLLOW THESE STEPS:
STEP 1: CONVERT THE MASS FROM KILOGRAMS TO GRAMS (2.5 KG = 2500 GRAMS).
STEP 2: DETERMINE THE VOLUME OF THE STAINLESS STEEL BAR IN CUBIC CENTIMETERS. (VOLUME = LENGTH X WIDTH X HEIGHT).
STEP 3: MULTIPLY THE VOLUME BY THE DENSITY OF STAINLESS STEEL TO GET THE MASS IN GRAMS OF STAINLESS STEEL IN WATER. (MASS IN WATER = VOLUME X DENSITY).
STEP 4: CONVERT THE MASS IN GRAMS OF STAINLESS STEEL IN WATER TO KILOGRAMS BY DIVIDING BY 1000. (MASS IN SEAWATER = MASS IN WATER / 1000).
THE WEIGHT OF THE MISSING STAINLESS STEEL GUIDE BAR IN SEAWATER IS APPROXIMATELY 2.48 KILOGRAMS.
IF THE MISSING GUIDE BAR HAD SUNK TO THE BOTTOM OF THE OCEAN, IT WOULD HAVE WEIGHED APPROXIMATELY 2.5 KILOGRAMS OUT OF WATER BUT ONLY 2.48 KILOGRAMS IN SEAWATER.

INCIDENT 691143 - 076328C002 KARISH PROJECT - ACCIDENT - ENVIRONMENTAL SPILL FROM JD ASSISTER A FRAME HYDRAULICS

JD ASSISTER IN PORT FOR PLOUGH CHANGEOVER OPERATIONS AND INITIALLY STBD TO THE QUAY FOR GENERAL OPERATIONS AND ALSO TO DISEMBARK CREW THAT WOULD BE CARRYING OUT TASKS FOR THE ONLOADING OPERATION OF THE PLOUGH.
0747HRS, WHILST JD ASSISTER WAS STERN TO THE QUAYSIDE IN PREPARATION FOR LIFTING THE BACKFILL PLOUGH FROM QUAYSIDE TO VESSEL, A HYDRAULIC OIL LEAK FROM THE PORT SIDE OF THE A-FRAME OCCURRED.
THE LEAK CAME FROM THE AFT TOP PORT SIDE OF THE A-FRAME AND OIL WAS DISCHARGED ONTO THE QUAYSIDE.
ADDITIONALLY AT APPROX. 0810HRS AN ATTEMPT WAS MADE ONBOARD THE VESSEL TO HALT THE LEAK OF THE OIL FROM THE A-FRAME. A HATCH ON THE A-FRAME WAS OPENED AND HYDRAULIC OIL ESCAPED.
A SMALL AMOUNT OF OIL WAS SEEN IN THE WATER AT THE STERN OF THE VESSEL.
RIGGERS IMMEDIATELY USED THE READY TO USE SPILL KITS AND SHOVELS TO CREATE A DAM TO PREVENT OIL ESCAPING INTO THE WATER.
THE SHORESIDE TFMC OPS MANAGER WAS CONTACTED AT 0751HRS AND INFORMED OF THE LEAK AND FURTHER ASSISTANCE WAS REQUESTED AND RECEIVED WITH ADDITIONAL SPILL KITS SENT FROM TFMC BASE.
TFMC OPS MANAGER INFORMED DP WORLD AND GAC AGENT OF THE INCIDENT.
A REQUEST WAS MADE FOR A BOOM TO BE POSITIONED AROUND THE VESSEL STERN TO CONTAIN THE HYDRAULIC OIL IF REQUIRED. – COMPLETED.
EMAIL SENT TO DPW TO REQUEST THEIR INFORMING OF RELEVANT AUTHORITIES - COMPLETED.

ON ARRIVAL THE TFMC PERSONNEL COMMENCED THE DE-MOBILISATION OF PROJECT EQUIPMENT.
THE PORT CALL MANAGEMENT PLAN AND NSA MOBILISATION COVID 19 RESTRICTIONS DETAILED THAT WHEN THE CONTRACTORS NEEDED TO GET ACCESS TO THE NSA ALL NSA / TFMC CREW WOULD VACATE THE DECK.

ON COMPLETION OF THE TFMC PERSONNEL EXITING THE DECK THE DECK SUPERVISOR CALLED THE QUAYSIDE TFMC REP / ENGINEER BY RADIO INFORMING HIM THAT IT WAS CLEAR FOR THE HOT WORK CONTRACTORS TO ACCESS THE DECK, THIS HAPPENED OVER SEVERAL TIMES THROUGH THE NIGHTSHIFT AS THE WORK SCOPE DICTATED.
TFMC MANNED THE UNDER-DECK AREAS FOR FIRE WATCH PURPOSES AS THE CONTRACTORS WERE NOT ALLOWED TO ACCESS THIS AREA DUE TO CURRENT COVID 19 RESTRICTIONS.
IT WAS WHILE ONE OF THE RIGGERS WAS DOWN IN THE CAROUSEL CONDUCTING FIRE WATCH HE OBSERVED WATER DRIPPING DOWN FROM THE UNDERSIDE OF THE MAIN DECK.
TOOL USED : HE WAS USING A OXYGEN AND ACETYLENE CUTTING TORCH FOR BURNING OFF THE SEA FASTENINGS.
THIS WAS THEN REPORTED TO THE DECK SUPV / RIGGING SUPERVISOR.
THIS WAS THEN REPORTED TO THE OCM.
THE OCM INFORMED THE NSS CAPTAIN AND BP REPS OF THE DAMAGE INCIDENT.
REPAIR TO BE UNDERTAKEN TO THE DECK OF THE NSA BY TFMC / CONTRACTORS.

THE SYSTEM HPU WAS THEN TURNED OFF TO PREVENT ANY FURTHER DISCHARGE.
THE SYSTEM WAS THEN SAFELY RECOVERED TO DECK.
MOMENTARILY OPERATED TETHER IN FUNCTION TO PROVE THIS WAS NOT CAUSING THE LOSS OF OIL.
RETURNED THE ROV TO THE GARAGE.
HSE, CLIENT, OCM AND CAPTAIN INFORMED.
INVESTIGATION INITIATED TO DETERMINE CAUSE OF THE LEAK AND QUANTITY.
BURST HOSE WAS IDENTIFIED. GARAGE HOSE #5 MAIN MANIFOLD PORT 2A TO VEHICLE LATCH OPEN (PICTURE ATTACHED).
2.5 LITRES OF TELLUS 32 LOST TO THE SEA.
SYSTEM WAS TOPPED UP WITH OIL.
TESTS CARRIED OUT TO CONFIRM LEAK RECTIFIED AND NO FURTHER LEAKS WERE PRESENT.
FULL SET OF PRE-DIVE CHECKS COMPLETED.

ABS GIVEN A TASK BY THE CHIEF OFFICER (C/O) TO CONDUCT LIFTING OPERATIONS UTILIZING THE PROVISION CRANE. (HELICOPTER SUITS FROM THE QUAYSIDE)
A VISUAL CHECK WAS COMPLETED BY THE AB, WHO NOTED THAT THE CRANE WAS NOT IN REST POSITION.
A MANUALLY TEST OF THE BLOCK COMMENCED, WHERE IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE BLOCK WAS NOT LOWERING AND THE WIRE WAS SLACK.
THE AB DECIDED TO TAKE UP THE SLACK BUT NOTICED THAT THE WIRE WAS TWISTED AT THIS TIME.
THE CRANE WAS TURNED OFF AND AN INVESTIGATION COMMENCED, WHERE IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE WIRE WAS OUT OF THE SHEAVE AND JAMMED.
IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: CRANE TECHNICIAN WAS INFORMED OF THE INCIDENT AT 06.45 AM 20.07.2022.
THE SITE WAS ATTENDED AND CRANE BOOM WAS NOTED TO BE STUCK IN THE AIR.
OBSERVATIONS WERE MADE, SLACK WIRE AT WINCH AND LOAD OF THE HOOK WEIGHT WAS SUPPORTED BY THE SHEAVES.
WIRE ROPE HAD TWISTED ON ITSELF AND BIRD CAGED.
SOME OUTER STRAND PROTRUSIONS WERE EVIDENT IN OTHER AREAS.
NO FUNCTIONS COULD BE OPERATED (EXCEPT SLEW) AS THE WINCH LIMIT WAS ACTIVATED.
HYDRAULIC LIMIT WAS BYPASSED AND CRANE WAS MADE SAFE.
FOLLOW ON ACTIONS: ROPE WAS CONFIRMED TO BE JAMMED IN BETWEEN THE BOOM TIP KNUCKLE BOOM SHEAVES.
BOTH SHEAVES WERE REMOVED, CLEANED AND INSPECTED.
STORES VISITED TO CONFIRM SPARE PARTS OF 1 X ROPE AND 1 X SHEAVE IN STOCK.
OPTIONS DISCUSSED AND REPAIR DISCUSSED WITH CHIEF ENGINEER.
UPDATE ON REPLACEMENT BY THE CRANE TECH 21/07: REMOVED WIRE ROPE AND DISCARDED.
BOTH SHEAVES CLEANED AND FULLY INSPECTED.

RECOVERING THE PORT BELL AFTER COMPLETION OF DIVE NUMBER 24
THE LOSS OF PRESSURE READING FROM THE BELL INTERNAL DISPLAY WAS DUE TO ITS RESPECTIVE RING, EXTERNAL SEAL OF THE ROTARY UNION FAILING

TIME LINE CAN BE FOUND ON DIVE LOG

DIVE SUPERVISOR THEN INSTRUCTED THE DIVERS TO CLOSE THE 10 SAFETY CRITICAL VALVES

DIVE SUPERVISOR THEN CONTACTED OCM AND LSS AND REPORTED THAT HE HAD EXCEEDED EXCURSION BY 2M
DIVE TECHS THEN IMMEDIATELY BEGAN INVESTIGATION AS TO WHY THIS OCCURRED
THE INCIDENT DID NOT RESULT IN ANY DAMAGE TO THE SUBMERSIBLE OR ITS SYSTEMS
FOLLOW UP ACTIONS WERE TAKEN TO ENSURE THAT SUCH AN INCIDENT DOES NOT OCCUR AGAIN IN THE FUTURE

ACCIDENT 184 - DEEP DISCOVERER - SHELL CARRACK QA - 300626C001 - 05.02.2022 - TAUT-WIRE PARTED SUBSEA
HEADING WAS 223 DEGREES, VESSEL WAS IN ADP
WIND WAS 17.6KTS TO 23.6KTS DIRECTION OF WIND WAS FROM 230 DEGREES
SEA WAS ASSESSED AS HS 2.5M TO HMAX 4.0M

TASK / ACTIONS LEADING UP TO THE INCIDENT: ON COMPLETION OF AN INTERIM PORT CALL IN GREAT YARMOUTH (CREW CHANGE AND LOAD PROJECT EQUIPMENT), THE VESSEL ARRIVED BACK IN FIELD AND COMMENCED FIELD RE-ENTRY TRIALS.
INCIDENT / INITIAL FINDINGS: ON ARRIVAL IN THE FIELD THE VESSEL SET UP APPPROX. 1000M DOWN WEATHER FROM THE CARRACK PLATFORM AND CLEAR OF SUBSEA ASSETS.
THE VESSEL THEN CONFIGURED THE POWER MANAGEMENT SYSTEM AND THRUSTERS FOR DIVING OPERATIONS.
THE INITIAL PART OF THE TRIALS ENTAILS THE VESSEL COMING OFF DP TO TEST MANUAL CONTROLS ON BOTH BRIDGE WINGS AND FORWARD AND AFT STATIONS AND ALSO THE C-JOY JOYSTICK CONTROL AT DIFFERENT LOCATIONS.
THIS IS NORMAL PRACTICE AND THE VESSEL WOULD ALWAYS MOVE SOMEWHAT DOWN WEATHER DURING THESE TESTS.
THE DIFFERENCE THIS TIME WAS THE DISTANCE THE VESSEL MOVED DUE TO THE STRONG WEATHER CONDITIONS.

THE DPO’S HAD EXPECTED A GREATER CHANGE OF VESSEL POSITION DUE TO THE PREVAILING WEATHER AND HAD SET THE VESSEL UP WELL AWAY FROM CLIENT ASSETS, HOWEVER COMPOUNDED WITH THE CURRENT THE DRIFT TOOK A DIFFERENT ANGLE THAT WAS ANTICIPATED PUTTING THE VESSEL IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE SUBSEA UMBILICAL WHEN THE VESSEL WAS PUT BACK INTO DP.

AT APPROX. 16:43 WHEN THE PORT TAUT-WIRE WAS DEPLOYED FOR TESTING AND DURING RECOVERY IT IS ASSUMED THE WIRE SNAGGED SUBSEA, WHICH RESULTED IN THE WIRE PARTING AND THE DEPRESSOR WEIGHT REMAINING SUBSEA.

ON DISCOVERING THAT THE WIRE HAD PARTED, THE SURVEY SCREEN WAS REVIEWED, AND THE TAUT-WIRE WAS NOTED TO BE IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE CARRACK EAST WELL UMBILICAL, WHICH IS BELIEVED TO BE ROCK DUMPED OR POSSIBLY TRENCHED.
THE CAUSE OF THE SNAGGING TO BE INVESTIGATED ONCE SUITABLE WEATHER CONDITIONS ALLOW THE ROV TO RETURN TO OPERATIONS.
NOTE: THE WEIGHT OF THE DEPRESSOR WEIGHT IS 360KG

CURRENT SITUATION/INITIAL ACTION TAKEN: FOLLOWING ON FROM THE INCIDENT, ALL RELEVANT PERSONNEL WERE INFORMED INCLUDING THE MASTER, OCM, ONBOARD CLIENT REPS AND HSEA WITH THOSE ONSHORE ALSO NOTIFIED ACCORDINGLY (PROJECT MANAGER, ASSET MANAGER ETC). THE TAUT-WIRE WILL BE REPLACED, AND A SPARE DEPRESSOR WEIGHT WILL BE INSTALLED.
THE RE-ENTRY TRIALS WERE COMPLETED, AND THE VESSEL IS CURRENTLY DOWN FOR WEATHER IN OPEN WATER OUTSIDE OF THE PLATFORMS 500M ZONE.
COMMENTS: THE WIRE HAS BEEN REPLACED AND SPARE WEIGHT INSTALLED.
INCIDENT WITNESS ACCOUNT FORMS ARE BEING COLLATED AND WILL BE ATTACHED WITHIN THE CASE.
THE CAUSE OF THE SNAGGING WILL BE INVESTIGATED ONCE SUITABLE WEATHER CONDITIONS ALLOW THE ROV TO RETURN TO OPERATIONS.

TASK LEADING UP TO THE INCIDENT: AFTER COMPLETION OF UMBILICAL INITIATION THROUGH THE PIPELAY TOWER AND INSTALLATION OF BEND RESTRICTORS ON THE PRODUCT THE VESSEL COMMENCED DEPLOYMENT TO DEPTH
PIPE WAS PAID OUT WITH UPPER TENSIONER ONLY AT STEADY SPEED OF ~7.3M/MIN WITH REEL OPERATED LOCALLY
IT WAS NOTICED THAT THE REEL TENDS TO “JUMP” ON THE UNDER ROLLER, REPOSITIONING SIDEWAYS DUE TO UNEVEN LOAD DISTRIBUTION ON THE REEL, WITH MAJORITY OF PAYLOAD TO ONE SIDE
AT 02:00 FLUID WAS NOTICED TO BE SPRAYING AT THE REEL AFTER A JUMP OF THE REEL
HALLIBURTON REPORTED A LOSS OF PRESSURE OF 2,300PSI IN THE PRODUCT (FROM 2,500PSI OPERATIONAL TO 200PSI) THROUGH REMOTE MONITORING

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS TAKEN: AN ALL STOP CALLED INCIDENT WAS IMMEDIATELY REPORTED TO ONBOARD PE ,OCS, SHELL CLIENT REPRESENTATIVE, HSE, BRIDGE FLUID WAS CLEANED UP, COUPLINGS TIGHTENED AND SIMILAR COUPLINGS CHECKED
COMMENTS: ON RESUMPTION THE SAME HAPPENED TWICE MORE BUT FROM DIFFERENT COUPLINGS

THESE FITTING CONNECTIONS AND WHOLE MANIFOLD ASSEMBLY WERE GOOD PRIOR THE INCIDENT AS IT WAS HIGH-PRESSURE-TESTED TOGETHER WITH UMBILICAL AS PART OF POST LOADOUT PRESSURE TESTING ACTIVITY 15K PSI (1034 BAR) TEST PRESSURE AND WAS HOLDING 4 HOURS 1% DROP AS PER ISO 13628-5 AND AS PER MANUFACTURER STANDARDS. IT PASSED AND ACCEPTED BY CLIENT
NO PERSONNEL WERE IN THE AREA OF THE PRESSURE RELEASE AS IT WAS BARRICADED FOR UMBILICAL INSTALLATION WORKS FROM REEL TOWARDS TOWER
THE FLUID SPILL WAS CONTAINED WITH SPILL KITS THE SPILL AREA WAS A SMALL AREA UNDER UMBILICAL WHEEL (CENTRE OF BACK DECK)
APPROX 2 GALLONS (8 LITRES) LOST TO DECK

POSSIBLE CAUSES: IMPROPER ALIGNMENT BETWEEN UNDER-ROLLER AND THE REEL MADE IT MOVE A LITTLE “SIDEWAYS”. UNEVEN LOAD ON REEL CONTIBUTES FURTHER TO THIS CAUSE WHICH IN THE END MADE IT “JUMPED” BACK TO ITS ORIGINAL POSITION AFTER FEW REVOLUTIONS

ACTIONS: STOP ALL WORK. TIME OUT FOR SAFETY CARRIED OUT. THEN BELOW ACTIONS TAKEN: 1) ISOLATE ALL UMBILICAL HOSES ON EACH OF THE 3 QTY OF MANIFOLDS. THIS IS TO PREVENT LOST PRESSURE FROM WITHIN UMBILICAL. 2) DEPRESSURIZE RESIDUE PRESSURE AND FLUID WITHIN THE MANIFOLD BLOCK TO ZERO BAR. (IT WAS ALREADY ZERO, ONCE WE ISOLATED THE UMBILICAL HOSES FROM THE MANIFOLD BLOCK, SINCE IT HAS BEEN LEAKING). 3) TIGHTEN ALL FITTINGS, LEAKED ONES AND NON-LEAKING ONES JUST TO GIVE ASSURANCE. 4) LINE UP THOSE UMBILICAL HOSES BACK ONLINE WITH THE MANIFOLD

NEAR MISS 546552 - NON-TECHNIP OWNED - BNJ-NM 14 - 2529 TAP PROJECT - GREECE/KP 350+500
1 YEAR DECLARED EXPERIENCE ON HYDRAULIC SIDEBOOMS
PASSED SAFETY INDUCTION AND SIDEBOOM OPERATOR TRAINING COURSE
FILLED IN THE PROJECT OPERATOR’S QUESTIONNAIRE
THE SIDEBOOM OPERATOR STATED THAT DURING THE MONTH THAT HE HAD BEEN ENGAGED ON THE TAP PROJECT HE HAD OPERATED THREE DIFFERENT TYPES OF SIDEBOOMS: CAT, KOMATSU AND EPH

THE SIDEBOOM OPERATOR STATED THAT HE HAD BEEN OPERATING THIS SPECIFIC EPH SIDEBOOM FOR THE PAST THREE DAYS, BUT HE HAD ALREADY OPERATED THE SAME MODEL FOR A FEW WEEKS WHILST WORKING ON THE TAP PROJECT
THE SIDEBOOM OPERATOR HAD BEEN WITH THE SAME TIE-IN CREW SINCE JOINING THE TAP PROJECT
NO SLOPE INCLINATION SIGNS WERE POSTED
THE TIE-IN SUPERVISOR HAD NOT ATTENDED ANY SPECIFIC STEEP SLOPE TRAINING
THE TIE-IN CREW WERE WORKING APPROXIMATELY 200 METRES AWAY FROM WHERE THE INCIDENT OCCURRED (OUT OF THE LINE OF FIRE)
THE INCIDENT OCCURRED AT 19°, THE SIDEBOOM ARRESTED ITS UNCONTROLLED DESCENT AT 14°
THE SIDEBOOM HAD BEEN USED EXTENSIVELY IN THE MORNING
THE CATERPILLAR C13 ENGINE RPM IS SET AT 2,100
IF THIS EXCEEDS 2,400 RPM A WARNING APPEARS AND AT 2,500 RPM THE ENGINE GOES INTO A ‘SAFETY MODE’ TO PROTECT ITSELF FROM PERMANENT DAMAGE WHICH RESULTED IN REDUCED POWER

AS THE MACHINE WAS NEGOTIATING A STEEP SLOPE AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT, THE REDUCED ENGINE POWER RESULTED IN THE ENGINE STALLING, CAUSING THE MACHINE TO MOMENTARILY FREEWHEEL FORWARDS DOWN THE SLOPE

BEST HEADING WAS EVALUATED TO BE 030 DEG AT THE TIME OF OVERBOARDING.
ENVIRONMENT TOTAL WAS FROM 060 DEG APROX.
VESSEL ASTERN MOVEMENT TRIAL CONDUCTED WITH POSITIVE RESULTS - SOZ IDENTIFIED PITCH WAS UP TO +/ 2DEG BUT VESSEL MOVEMENT AND HEADING CHANGE REDUCED IT TO +/- 1DEG BETWEEN MAX SWELL PERIODS OBSERVED.
DP TREND HEAVE AND PITCH MONITORED AND MINIMUM SWELL PERIOD CALCULATED TO BE 4 TO 6 MINUTES.
WIND WAS 045 18 KNOTS WITH A 2M SWELL, VISIBILITY WAS PARTLY CLOUDY.
WEATHER HAD BEEN ASSESSED OVER 24 HOUR PERIOD. 1700 HOURS WEATHER FORECAST REVIEWED.
LIFT PLAN AND MOC DISCUSSED AND APPROVED.
TAGLINE MANAGEMENT PLAN IN PLACE AND DISCUSSED.

TOOL BOX TALK WAS CONDUCTED PRIOR TO LIFT DISCUSSING IN DETAIL THE LIFT, POSITIONING OF PERSONNEL, TAGLINES, TUGGERS, MOVING THE LOAD, VESSEL MOTIONS, COMMUNICATION, SAFE ZONES, AND EVACUATION ROUTES IN CASE OF EMERGENCY.
TOFS LINE OF FIRE CONDUCTED ON PREVIOUS SHIFT.
TRA REVIEWED AND DISCUSSED IN DETAIL WITH CREW.
CRANE RADIUS PRE-RECORDED FOR CONNECTION AND INITIAL LIFT.
USE OF 2X CRANE TUGGERS - BOTH IN MANUAL MODE DISCUSSED.
PROCEDURE FOR RELYING DP TREND ESTABLISHED.
POSITIONS OF TUGGERS AND TAGLINES EVALUATED AND DEEMED TO BE IN BEST POSITIONS POSSIBLE.

AFTER COMPLETING ALL PREPARATORY WORKS, CONNECTING THE CRANE TO SSIV RIGGING, AND RELAYING DP TREND/PERIOD TO DECK, THE CREW COMMENCED THE LIFT OF THE 117 TE, 30M LONG SSIV FROM THE DECK OF THE SKANDI SKANSEN.
BOTH TUGGERS WERE CONNECTED IN MANUAL MODE, AND TAGLINES CONNECTED AS PER PLAN.
DURING INITIAL LIFT, THE FWD SSIV FRAME LIFTED FIRST AS EXPECTED, ALTHOUGH SLIGHTLY HIGHER THAN EXPECTED BEFORE STERN LIFTED, THE LIFT APPEARED TO BE STABLE.
THE CRANE TUGGERS WERE AT SUCH AN ANGLE THAT THEY WERE INEFFECTIVE DURING LIFT AND WOULD NOT BE EFFECTIVE UNTIL THE SSIV WAS AT BULWARK HEIGHT.

ONCE THE SSIV WAS OFF DECK (600MM TO 1000MM ON CRANE WIRE) AND THE CRANE STARTED TO SLEW LEFT/INCREASE RADIUS, AN UNEXPECTED SWELL SEQUENCE CAUSED THE VESSEL TO PITCH WHICH IN TURN CAUSED THE SSIV TO START SWINGING.
THE LEFT CRANE TUGGER WINCH CAUGHT THE SWING BUT IN TURN CAUSED THE FWD TO ROTATE FURTHER TO PORT AND THE SSIV TO SWING MORE VIOLENTLY.
THE SSIV SWUNG VIOLENTLY, CAUSING IT TO COLLIDE WITH THE CRANE BOOM AND THE VESSEL'S BULWARK.
THE COLLISION CAUSED SIGNIFICANT DAMAGE TO BOTH THE SSIV AND THE CRANE.
PERSONNEL ON BOARD WERE ABLE TO SECURE THE SSIV AND PREVENT FURTHER DAMAGE.
THE INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE RELEVANT AUTHORITIES AND INVESTIGATIONS ARE ONGOING.

ACCIDENT 517366 - EQUIPMENT DAMAGE - MHN 033968C001 - SKANDI AFRICA - 26.11.2016 - SHEARED BOLT ON TLS TREM TENSIONER 1
SMOOTH / WAVELETS 0.1M – 0.5M, SOUTH WESTERLY MODERATE BREEZE 11-16KTS, PARTIALLY CLOUDY

AT 15.00PM (APPROX.) ON 26.11.2016 THE VESSEL WAS ON THE MOHO NORD PROJECT INFIELD ON DP AT COORDINATES 05.13 1°S 011°18.7’ E; THE SEA STATE WAS ASSESSED AS SMOOTH / WAVELETS 0.1M – 0.5M, WIND DIRECTION WAS SOUTH WESTERLY MODERATE BREEZE 11-16KTS, VISIBILITY WAS PARTIALLY CLOUDY

THE TLS TECHNICIAN WAS CARRYING OUT A ROUTINE INSPECTION ON THE TLS WHEN HE OBSERVED A SHEARED BOLT ON THE BOTTOM JUNCTION OF THE TREM (TENSIONER RETRACT & EXTEND MECHANISM) 1 CYLINDER STARBOARD SIDE OF THE UPPER TLS TENSIONER.
THE 24MM BOLT HAS SHEARED AND DETACHED FROM THE HOUSING, NO POTENTIAL FOR DROPS AS THE HEAD OF THE BOLT IS WIRE-LOCKED.

CP EVALUATED THE DAMAGE AND GENERATED A DAMAGE LOSS REPORT (ATTACHED TO THE CASE). JRA PERFORMED FOR THE BOLT REPLACEMENT AND BOLT REPLACED BY THE TLS TECHNICIANS. ALL OTHER SIMILAR FIXINGS CHECKED FOR SECURITY.

THE INITIAL INVESTIGATION HAS HIGHLIGHTED THE FOLLOWING: IT WOULD APPEAR THAT THERE MAY BE AN ISSUE WITH THE LUBRICATION OF THE BOTTOM JUNCTION, CPE FORWARDED THE INFORMATION TO HUISMAN FOR INVESTIGATION AND ANALYSIS.
DURING THE BOLT REPLACEMENT IT WAS POSSIBLE TO MOVE THE THE PIN WITH A CROSS BAR. SO THE LUBRICATION DON'T SEEMS TO BE THE ROOT CAUSE.
IT'S MORE LIKELY THAT THE BOLT HAS BEEN OVER TORQUE DURING INSTALLATION.
ACCORDING TO THE PICTURES THE FRACTURE SURFACE DOES NOT SHOW TYPICAL FATIGUE DAMAGE NOR DOES IT SHOW TENSIONAL OVERLOAD FAILURE, INSTANT SHEAR FAILURE DUE TO SIGNIFICANT OVERLOAD SEEMS PLAUSIBLE.
WE AGREE WITH TECHNIP THAT INSUFFICIENT GREASING COULD HAVE CAUSED SHAFT ROTATION AND FINALLY THIS FAILURE.
WE RECOMMEND TO CONTINUE REGULAR GREASING AND BOLT INSPECTIONS (AS PER STANDARD / OPERATIONAL INTERVAL) AND REVERT IN CASE SIMILAR FAILURE OCCURS IN THE FUTURE.
IN THAT CASE HUISMAN WILL BE NOTIFIED AND ANALYSIS WILL BE CARRIED OUT.

THE TASK WAS TO CUT THE TWO HOLD BACK WIRES TO RELEASE THE 2ND END FLET WINGS. A SAFETY LANYARD IS ATTACHED TO THE OTS VEHICLE PRIOR TO CUTTING THE SLING.
TWO WIRE ROPE SLINGS HAVE TO BE CUT TO RELEASE THE WING. EACH WIRE ROPE SLING HAS ONE SECONDARY LANYARD (COMPRISING OF A SOFT SLING) AND ONE RECOVERY LOOP ATTACHED.

AFTER CUTTING THE TWO HOLD BACK WIRES TO RELEASE THE WINGS ON THE 2ND END FLET WITH BOTH WIRES SECURED ON THE OTS ROV SHACKLE, THE ROV FLEW BACK TO THE GARAGE TO STORE THEM ON THE GARAGE SHACKLE. ON THE WAY THE TWO WIRE SLINGS AND THE TWO SOFT SLINGS BECOME ENTANGLED SO THE ROV STOPPED TO UNTANGLE THEM.

THIS OPERATION WAS MADE MORE CHALLENGING BECAUSE THE OTS FIVE FUNCTION ARM WAS HOLDING THE 75MM HYDRAULIC CUTTER WHICH MEANT ONLY THE SEVEN FUNCTION SCHILLING ARM WAS AVAILABLE TO UNTANGLE THE TWO SOFT STROPS AND WIRE SLINGS REMOVED FROM THE FLET WINGS.
HAD THE WIRES BEEN CUT AND RECOVERED ONE AT A TIME, IT WOULD HAVE AVOIDED THE WIRE BECOMING ENTANGLED.
STIFFER LOOPS ON THE SOFT SLINGS WOULD HAVE MADE IT EASIER FOR THE ROVS TO PLACE THE LOOPS ON THE HOOKS OR SHACKLES.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS TAKEN: A LINEAR SURVEY WAS CARRIED OUT ALONG +200 METER TO -200 METERS OF THE UMBILICAL FROM THE INITIAL DROPS POINT, CORRESPONDING TO 10% OF THE WATER DEPTH. A FURTHER CIRCULAR SURVEY AROUND THE DROPS AREA ALSO CARRIED OUT HOWEVER NO RIGGING OR DAMAGE TO THE UMBILICAL WAS IDENTIFIED.
